verses.12:27: Consider the lilies, how they grow: they do not labor, nor do they spin; yet I say to you, not even Solomon in all his glory was dressed like one of these.
verses.12:28: Now if God thus clothes the grass, which today is in the field and tomorrow is thrown into the oven, how much more you, of little faith?
verses.12:29: And you, do not seek what you will eat or what you will drink, and do not be lifted up on high;
verses.12:30: for the nations of the world seek all these things, yet your Father knows that you are in need of these things.
verses.12:31: Nevertheless, seek first the kingdom of God and His righteousness, and all these things will be added to you.
verses.12:32: Do not fear, little flock, because it has pleased your Father to give you the kingdom.
verses.12:33: Sell the things you possess and give alms. Make for yourselves purses that do not grow old, an unfailing treasure in the heavens, where no thief approaches, nor does a moth destroy.
verses.12:34: For where your treasure is, there your heart will also be.
verses.12:35: Let your loins be girded and lamps burning in your hands,
verses.12:36: and you yourselves be like people waiting for their master when he returns from the wedding, so that when he comes and knocks, they may immediately open to him.
verses.12:37: Blessed are those servants whom the master, when he comes, will find watching. Amen, I tell you that he will gird himself and make them recline at table, and passing along he will serve them.
verses.12:38: And if he comes in the second watch, and if he comes in the third watch, and finds them so, blessed are those servants.
verses.12:39: Now know this, that if the head of the household knew at what hour the thief was coming, he would surely keep watch and would not permit his house to be broken through.
verses.12:40: And you also, be ready, because at an hour you do not expect, the Son of Man will come."
verses.12:41: Then Peter said to Him, "Lord, are You speaking this parable to us, or also to everyone?"
verses.12:42: And the Lord said, "Who, do you think, is the faithful and prudent steward whom the master has appointed over his household, to give them the measure of wheat at the proper time?
verses.12:43: Blessed is that servant whom the master, when he comes, will find doing so.
verses.12:44: Truly I say to you that he will appoint him over all the things he possesses.
verses.12:45: But if that servant says in his heart, 'My master is delaying in coming,' and begins to beat the servants and maidservants, and to eat and to drink and to become drunk,
verses.12:46: the master of that servant will come on a day he does not expect and at an hour he does not know, and will sever him and place his portion with the unfaithful.
verses.12:47: Now that servant who knew the will of his master, and did not prepare, and does not act according to his will, will be beaten with many blows;
verses.12:48: but the one who did not know and did things deserving blows will be beaten with few. Now from everyone to whom much has been given, much will be required, and from the one to whom they have entrusted much, they will ask more.
verses.12:49: I have come to cast fire onto the earth, and what do I want except that it be kindled?
verses.12:50: But I have a baptism with which to be baptized, and how constrained am I until it is completed?
verses.12:51: Do you think that I have come to give peace on the earth? No, I say to you, but separation;
verses.12:52: for from now on five in one house will be divided; three against two and two against three
verses.12:53: will be divided: father against son and son against his father, mother against daughter and daughter against mother, mother-in-law against her daughter-in-law and daughter-in-law against her mother-in-law."
verses.12:54: Now He was also saying to the crowds, "When you see a cloud rising from the west, at once you say, 'A rainstorm is coming,' and so it happens.
verses.12:55: And when the south wind is blowing, you say, 'There will be intense heat,' and it happens.
verses.12:56: Hypocrites! You know how to discern the face of the sky and the earth, yet how do you not discern this time?
verses.12:57: And why even on your own do you not judge what is right?
verses.12:58: Now as you go with your adversary to the ruler, on the way make an effort to be freed from him, so that he might not drag you to the judge, and the judge hand you over to the bailiff, and the bailiff throw you into prison.
verses.12:59: I say to you, you will not come out from there until you pay back even the very last mite."
verses.13:1: Now some people were present at that very time, reporting to Him about the Galileans whose blood Pilate mixed with their sacrifices.
verses.13:2: And answering, He said to them, "Do you think that these Galileans were sinners beyond all Galileans because they suffered such things?
verses.13:3: No, I tell you; but unless you have repentance, you will all perish in the same way.
verses.13:4: Like those eighteen on whom the tower in Siloam fell and killed them, do you think that they too were debtors beyond all the people living in Jerusalem?
verses.13:5: No, I tell you; but if you do not repent, you will all perish in the same way."
verses.13:6: Now He was also telling this parable: "A certain man had a fig tree planted in his vineyard, and he came looking for fruit on it and found none.
verses.13:7: So he said to the keeper of the vineyard, 'Look, it is three years now that I have been coming looking for fruit on this fig tree, and I find none. Cut it down, therefore; why does it even occupy the ground?'
verses.13:8: But answering, he says to him, 'Sir, leave it alone this year as well, until I dig around it and put down manure,
verses.13:9: and if indeed it bears fruit—but if not, in the future you will cut it down.'"
verses.13:10: Now He was teaching in their synagogue on the Sabbaths.
verses.13:11: And look, there was a woman who had a spirit of infirmity for eighteen years, and she was bent over and could not look upward at all.
verses.13:12: When Jesus saw her, He called her to Himself and said to her, "Woman, you are released from your infirmity."
verses.13:13: And He placed His hands on her, and immediately she was straightened up and was glorifying God.
verses.13:14: But answering, the synagogue leader, indignant because Jesus had healed on the Sabbath, was saying to the crowd, "There are six days in which one ought to work; therefore come on those days and be healed, and not on the Sabbath day."
verses.13:15: But the Lord, answering him, said, "Hypocrites! Does not each one of you untie his ox or donkey from the manger on the Sabbath and lead it to water?
verses.13:16: And ought not this daughter of Abraham, whom Satan bound—look, for eighteen years—to be untied from this bond on the Sabbath day?"
verses.13:17: And as He was saying these things, all His adversaries were ashamed, and all the people were rejoicing over all the things that were gloriously being done by Him.
verses.13:18: Therefore He was saying, "What is the kingdom of God like, and what will I reckon it to be like?
verses.13:19: It is like a grain of mustard seed that a man took and put into his garden, and it grew and turned into a large tree, and the birds of the sky rested in its branches."
verses.13:20: And again He said, "What will I reckon the kingdom of God to be like?
verses.13:21: It is like leaven that a woman took and hid in three measures of flour, until all of it was leavened."
verses.13:22: And He was going through cities and villages, teaching and making His journey to Jerusalem.
verses.13:23: Now someone said to Him, "Lord, are there few who are being saved?" And He said to them,
verses.13:24: "Strive to enter through the narrow gate, because many, I tell you, will seek to enter and will not be able.
verses.13:25: Once the master of the house has entered and closed the door, you will begin to stand outside and knock on the door, saying, 'Lord, open for us,' and answering, He will say to you, 'I do not know you, where you are from.'
verses.13:26: Then you will begin to say, 'We ate and drank in Your presence, and You taught in our streets.'
verses.13:27: And He will say to you, 'I do not know you, where you are from; depart from Me, all you workers of unrighteousness.'
verses.13:28: In that place there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth, when you see Abraham and Isaac and Jacob and all the prophets in the kingdom of God, but yourselves being driven outside.
verses.13:29: And they will come from the east and the west, and the north and the south, and will recline at table in the kingdom of God.
verses.13:30: And look, there are last ones who will be first, and there are first ones who will be last."
verses.13:31: On that very day, some of the Pharisees came up, saying to Him, "Leave and go away from here, because Herod wants to kill You."
verses.13:32: And He said to them, "Go and tell that fox, 'Look, I drive out demons and perform healings today and tomorrow, and on the third day I am brought to completion.'
verses.13:33: Nevertheless, I must journey today and tomorrow and the following day, because it is not possible for a prophet to perish outside Jerusalem.
verses.13:34: Jerusalem, Jerusalem, who kills the prophets and stones those who are sent to you, how often did I want to gather your children, just as a bird gathers her brood under her wings, and you were unwilling?
verses.13:35: Look, your house will be left desolate to you. And I tell you that you will not see Me until the time comes when you will say, 'Blessed is the One who comes in the name of the Lord.'"
verses.14:1: And it happened, when Jesus entered the house of a certain leader of the Pharisees on the Sabbath to eat bread, that they themselves were watching Him.
verses.14:2: And look, a certain man with dropsy was before Him.
verses.14:3: And answering, Jesus spoke to the experts in the law and the Pharisees, saying, "Is it lawful to heal on the Sabbath?"
verses.14:4: But they remained silent. Then He took hold of him, healed him, and sent him away.
verses.14:5: And answering them, He said, "If any one of you has a donkey or an ox fall into a well, will he not immediately pull it out on the Sabbath day?"
verses.14:6: And they were not able to reply to Him about these things.
verses.14:7: Now He was also telling a parable to those who were invited, noticing how they were choosing the first places at table, saying to them,
verses.14:8: "When you are invited to a wedding feast, do not recline in the first place, in case someone more honored than you has been invited by him,
verses.14:9: and the one who called you and him comes and says to you, 'Give place to this man,' and then with shame you begin to take the last place.
verses.14:10: But when you are called, go and recline in the last place, so that when the one who invited you comes, he may say to you, 'Friend, go up higher.' Then you will have glory in the presence of those reclining together,
verses.14:11: because everyone who exalts himself will be humbled, and the one who humbles himself will be exalted."
verses.14:12: Now He was also saying to the one who had invited Him, "When you give a lunch or a dinner, do not call your friends, nor your brothers, nor your relatives, nor rich neighbors, in case they too invite you back and repayment is made to you;
verses.14:13: but when you give a banquet, call the poor, the disabled, the lame, and the blind,
verses.14:14: and you will be blessed, because they do not have the means to repay you; for you will be repaid at the resurrection of the righteous."
verses.14:15: When one of those reclining together heard these things, he said to Him, "Blessed is the one who will eat bread in the kingdom of God."
verses.14:16: But He said to him, "A certain man prepared a great dinner and called many.
verses.14:17: And at the hour of dinner he sent his servant to tell those who had been invited to come, because everything is now ready.
verses.14:18: And all of them together began to make excuses. The first said to him, 'I have bought a farm, and I need to go out and see it; I ask you, consider me excused.'
verses.14:19: And another said, 'I have bought five yoke of oxen, and I am going to test them; I ask you, consider me excused.'
verses.14:20: And another said, 'I have married a wife, and therefore I cannot come.'
verses.14:21: And returning, the servant reported these things to his master. Then the master of the house, angry, said to his servant, 'Go out quickly into the streets and lanes of the city, and bring in here the poor, the disabled, the blind, and the lame.'
verses.14:22: And the servant said, 'Master, it has been done as you commanded, and there is still room.'
verses.14:23: And the master said to the servant, 'Go out into the roads and hedges and compel them to enter, so that my house may be filled.
verses.14:24: And I tell you that none of those men who were called will taste my dinner.'"
verses.14:25: Now many crowds were going with Him, and turning around, He said to them,
verses.14:26: "If anyone comes to Me and does not hate his father and mother, and wife and children, and brothers and sisters, and even his own life as well, he cannot be My disciple.
verses.14:27: And whoever does not carry his cross and come after Me cannot be My disciple.
verses.14:28: For which one of you, wanting to build a tower, does not first sit down and calculate the expenses that are necessary, to see whether he has enough to finish it,
verses.14:29: so that, after he has laid the foundation and is not able to finish, all who see it may not begin to mock him,
verses.14:30: saying, 'This man began to build and was not able to complete it'?
verses.14:31: Or what king, about to go wage war against another king, does not first sit down and consider whether he is able with ten thousand to meet the one who comes against him with twenty thousand?
verses.14:32: Otherwise, while the other is still far away, sending a delegation, he asks for the things that pertain to peace.
verses.14:33: In the same way, therefore, every one of you who does not renounce all that he possesses cannot be My disciple.
verses.14:34: Salt is good; but if salt has lost its flavor, with what will it be seasoned?
verses.14:35: It is useful neither for the soil nor for the manure pile; instead, it will be thrown outside. The one who has ears to hear, let him hear."
verses.15:1: Now tax collectors and sinners were drawing near to Him in order to hear Him.
verses.15:2: And the Pharisees and scribes were murmuring, saying, "This man welcomes sinners and eats with them."
verses.15:3: And He spoke this parable to them, saying,
verses.15:4: "What man among you, who has one hundred sheep, and if he loses one of them, does not leave the ninety-nine in the wilderness and go after the one that was lost until he finds it?
verses.15:5: And when he finds it, he places it on his shoulders, rejoicing,
verses.15:6: and coming home, he calls together his friends and neighbors, saying to them, 'Rejoice with me, because I have found my sheep that was lost.'
verses.15:7: I tell you that in this way there will be joy in heaven over one sinner who repents, rather than over ninety-nine righteous ones who do not need repentance.
verses.15:8: Or what woman, having ten drachmas, if she loses one drachma, does not light a lamp and sweep the house and search diligently until she finds it?
verses.15:9: And when she finds it, she calls together her friends and neighbors, saying, 'Rejoice with me, because I have found the drachma that I had lost.'
verses.15:10: In this way, I tell you, there will be joy before the angels of God over one sinner who repents."
verses.15:11: Then He said, "A certain man had two sons,
verses.15:12: and the younger of them said to his father, 'Father, give me the portion of the property that falls to me.' And he divided the property between them.
verses.15:13: And not many days later, having gathered everything together, the younger son traveled abroad into a distant region, and there he squandered his property by living dissolutely.
verses.15:14: And after he had spent everything, a severe famine arose in that region, and he himself began to be in need.
verses.15:15: And he went and attached himself to one of the citizens of that region, and he sent him to his farm to feed pigs.
verses.15:16: And he longed to fill his belly with the pods that the pigs were eating, and no one gave him any.
verses.15:17: Then coming back to himself, he said, 'How many hired workers in my father's house have an abundance of bread, while I am perishing here from hunger!
verses.15:18: I will rise and go to my father, and say to him, "Father, I have sinned against heaven and before you.
verses.15:19: I am no longer worthy to be called your son; make me like one of your hired workers."'
verses.15:20: And rising, he came to his father. Now while he was still far off, his father saw him and was moved with compassion, and running up, he fell on his neck and kissed him.
verses.15:21: And the son said to him, 'Father, I have sinned against heaven and before you. I am no longer worthy to be called your son.'
verses.15:22: But the father said to his servants, 'Quickly bring out the finest robe and clothe him in it, and put a ring on his hand and sandals on his feet;
verses.15:23: and bring the fattened calf and slaughter it, and let us eat and feast,
verses.15:24: because this son of mine was dead and has come back to life; he was lost and has been found.' And they began to feast.
verses.15:25: Now his older son was in the field, and as he was coming and drawing near to the house, he heard music and dancing.
verses.15:26: And he called one of the servants and asked what these things were.
verses.15:27: And he said to him, 'Your brother has come, and your father has slaughtered the fattened calf, because he has received him back safe.'
verses.15:28: But he became indignant and was unwilling to go in. Therefore his father came out and began to plead with him.
verses.15:29: But answering, he said to his father, 'Look, for so many years I have been serving you, and I have never disregarded your command, and yet you have never given me a young goat so that I might feast with my friends.
verses.15:30: But after this son of yours came, who devoured his property with prostitutes, you slaughtered the fattened calf for him.'
verses.15:31: And he said to him, 'Son, you are always with me, and everything that is mine is yours;
verses.15:32: yet it was fitting to feast and rejoice, because this brother of yours was dead and has come back to life; he was lost and has been found.'"
verses.16:1: Now He was also saying to His disciples, "There was a certain rich man who had a steward, and this man was accused before him as though he had squandered his possessions.
verses.16:2: And he called him and said to him, 'What is this that I hear about you? Render an account of your stewardship, for you will no longer be able to act as steward.'
verses.16:3: Then the steward said within himself, 'What am I to do, since my master is taking the stewardship away from me? I am not strong enough to dig; I am ashamed to beg.
verses.16:4: I know what I will do, so that when I am removed from the stewardship, they may receive me into their houses.'
verses.16:5: So having called together his master's debtors one by one, he said to the first, 'How much do you owe my master?'
verses.16:6: And he said, 'One hundred jars of oil.' And he said to him, 'Take your bond, and sit down quickly; write fifty.'
verses.16:7: Then he said to another, 'And you, how much do you owe?' And he said, 'One hundred cors of wheat.' He said to him, 'Take your document and write eighty.'
verses.16:8: And the master praised the unjust steward because he had acted prudently; for the sons of this age are more prudent than the sons of light in their own generation.
verses.16:9: And I say to you, make friends for yourselves from the mammon of injustice, so that when you fail, they may receive you into the eternal dwellings.
verses.16:10: The one who is faithful in what is least is also faithful in what is greater, and the one who is unjust in what is small is also unjust in what is greater.
verses.16:11: If therefore you have not been faithful in unjust mammon, who will entrust to you what is true?
verses.16:12: And if you have not been faithful in what belongs to another, who will give you what is yours?
verses.16:13: No servant can serve two masters; for either he will hate the one and love the other, or he will cling to the one and scorn the other. You cannot serve God and mammon."
verses.16:14: Now the Pharisees, who were greedy, were hearing all these things, and they were mocking Him.
verses.16:15: And He said to them, "You are the ones who justify yourselves before people, yet God knows your hearts; for what is lofty among people is an abomination before God.
verses.16:16: The Law and the Prophets were until John; from that time the kingdom of God is proclaimed as good news, and everyone presses forcefully into it.
verses.16:17: Yet it is easier for heaven and earth to pass away than for one pen-stroke from the Law to fall.
verses.16:18: Everyone who divorces his wife and marries another commits adultery, and the one who marries a woman divorced by her husband commits adultery.
verses.16:19: There was a certain rich man who was clothed in purple and fine linen and feasted splendidly every day.
verses.16:20: And there was a certain beggar named Lazarus, who lay at his gate, full of sores,
verses.16:21: longing to be satisfied with the crumbs that fell from the rich man's table, and no one gave him any; moreover, even the dogs came and licked his sores.
verses.16:22: Now it happened that the beggar died and was carried by the angels into Abraham's bosom. And the rich man also died and was buried in the underworld.
verses.16:23: And lifting up his eyes while he was in torments, he saw Abraham from a distance and Lazarus in his bosom.
verses.16:24: And crying out, he said, 'Father Abraham, have mercy on me and send Lazarus to dip the tip of his finger in water so that he may cool my tongue, because I am tormented in this flame.'
verses.16:25: And Abraham said to him, 'Son, remember that you received good things in your lifetime, and Lazarus likewise bad things; yet now he is comforted, whereas you are tormented;
verses.16:26: and besides all these things, a great chasm has been fixed between us and you, so that those who wish to pass from here to you cannot, nor cross over from there to here.'
verses.16:27: And he said, 'Then I beg you, father, to send him to my father's house,
verses.16:28: for I have five brothers, to testify to them so that they too may not come into this place of torments.'
verses.16:29: And Abraham said to him, 'They have Moses and the Prophets; let them listen to them.'
verses.16:30: But he said, 'No, father Abraham, yet if someone from the dead goes to them, they will repent.'
verses.16:31: Then he said to him, 'If they do not listen to Moses and the Prophets, neither will they believe if someone rises from the dead.'"
verses.17:1: And He said to His disciples, "It is impossible for stumbling blocks not to come, yet woe to the one through whom they come.
verses.17:2: It is more beneficial for him if a millstone is placed around his neck and he is thrown into the sea than for him to cause one of these little ones to stumble.
verses.17:3: Watch yourselves: if your brother sins against you, rebuke him; and if he repents, forgive him.
verses.17:4: And if he sins against you seven times in a day, and seven times in a day turns back to you, saying, 'I repent,' forgive him."
verses.17:5: And the apostles said to the Lord, "Add to our faith."
verses.17:6: But the Lord said, "If you have faith like a grain of mustard seed, you will say to this mulberry tree, 'Be uprooted and be transplanted into the sea,' and it will obey you.
verses.17:7: Now who among you, having a servant plowing or herding, would say to him when he has returned from the field, 'Come over at once, recline at table,'
verses.17:8: and would not say to him, 'Prepare what I may dine on, and gird yourself, and serve me while I eat and drink, and after these things you will eat and drink'?
verses.17:9: Is he grateful to that servant because he did what he had commanded him?
verses.17:10: I do not think so. So you also, when you have done all the things that have been commanded you, say, 'We are useless servants; what we were obligated to do, we have done.'"
verses.17:11: And it happened, as He was going to Jerusalem, that He was passing through the midst of Samaria and Galilee.
verses.17:12: And as He was entering a certain village, ten leprous men met Him, who stood at a distance;
verses.17:13: and they raised their voice, saying, "Jesus, Master, have mercy on us."
verses.17:14: When He saw them, He said, "Go, show yourselves to the priests." And it happened, as they were going, that they were cleansed.
verses.17:15: Now one of them, when he saw that he was cleansed, turned back, magnifying God with a loud voice,
verses.17:16: and fell on his face before His feet, giving thanks; and this man was a Samaritan.
verses.17:17: And Jesus answered and said, "Were not ten cleansed? And where are the nine?
verses.17:18: No one was found to return and give glory to God except this foreigner."
verses.17:19: And He said to him, "Rise, go; because your faith has saved you."
verses.17:20: Now when He was asked by the Pharisees, "When does the kingdom of God come?" He answered them and said, "The kingdom of God does not come with observation;
verses.17:21: nor will they say, 'Look, here!' or 'Look, there!' For look, the kingdom of God is within you."
verses.17:22: And He said to His disciples, "Days will come when you will long to see one day of the Son of Man, and you will not see it.
verses.17:23: And they will say to you, 'Look, here!' and 'Look, there!' Do not go, nor follow after them;
verses.17:24: for just as lightning, flashing from under heaven to the places that are under heaven, shines, so will the Son of Man be in His day.
verses.17:25: First, however, He must suffer many things, and be rejected by this generation.
verses.17:26: And just as it happened in the days of Noah, so will it also be in the days of the Son of Man:
verses.17:27: they were eating and drinking, taking wives and being given in marriage, up to the day on which Noah entered the ark; and the flood came and destroyed them all.
verses.17:28: In the same way, just as it happened in the days of Lot: they were eating and drinking, buying and selling, planting and building;
verses.17:29: but on the day Lot went out from Sodom, it rained fire and sulfur from heaven and destroyed them all;
verses.17:30: just like this it will be on the day when the Son of Man is revealed.
verses.17:31: In that hour, let the one who is on the housetop, whose belongings are in the house, not come down to take them; and likewise, let the one who is in the field not turn back.
verses.17:33: Whoever seeks to save his life will lose it, and whoever loses it will give it life.
verses.17:34: I tell you, in that night two will be in one bed: one will be taken up, and the other will be left behind;
verses.17:35: two women will be grinding together: one will be taken up, and the other will be left behind; two in the field: one will be taken up, and the other will be left behind."
verses.17:37: And He said to them, "Wherever the body is, there the eagles will also be gathered."
verses.18:1: Now He was also speaking a parable to them, that it is necessary to pray always and not grow faint,
verses.18:2: saying, "A certain judge was in a certain city who did not fear God and did not respect man.
verses.18:3: And a certain widow was in that city, and she kept coming to him, saying, 'Vindicate me against my adversary.'
verses.18:4: And he was unwilling for a long time. After these things, however, he said within himself, 'Even though I do not fear God, nor do I respect man,
verses.18:5: yet because this widow is bothersome to me, I will vindicate her, so that in the end she does not come and bruise me.'"
verses.18:6: And the Lord said, "Hear what the judge of iniquity says.
verses.18:7: Now will God not carry out the vindication of His chosen ones who cry out to Him day and night, and will He have patience with them?
verses.18:8: I tell you that He will quickly carry out their vindication. Nevertheless, when the Son of Man comes, do you think He will find faith on the earth?"
verses.18:9: Now He also spoke this parable to certain ones who trusted in themselves as righteous and scorned the rest:
verses.18:10: "Two men ascended into the temple to pray: one was a Pharisee and the other a tax collector.
verses.18:11: Standing, the Pharisee was praying these things to himself, 'God, I give thanks to You because I am not like the rest of men: robbers, the unjust, adulterers, or even like this tax collector.
verses.18:12: I fast twice in the week; I give tithes of all things that I possess.'
verses.18:13: And the tax collector, standing far off, was unwilling even to lift his eyes toward heaven, but kept striking his chest, saying, 'God, be gracious to me, a sinner.'
verses.18:14: I tell you, this man went down into his house justified rather than that one; because everyone who exalts himself will be humbled, and the one who humbles himself will be exalted."
verses.18:15: Now they were also bringing infants to Him so that He might touch them. When the disciples saw this, they were rebuking them.
verses.18:16: But Jesus, calling them together, said, "Allow the children to come to Me, and do not forbid them, for the kingdom of God belongs to such ones.
verses.18:17: Amen, I tell you, whoever does not receive the kingdom of God like a child will not enter into it."
verses.18:18: And a certain ruler questioned Him, saying, "Good Teacher, by doing what will I possess eternal life?"
verses.18:19: But Jesus said to him, "Why do you call Me good? There is no one good except God alone.
verses.18:20: You know the commandments: you shall not kill; you shall not commit adultery; you shall not commit theft; you shall not speak false testimony; honor your father and mother."
verses.18:21: He said, "I have observed all these things from my youth."
verses.18:22: Upon hearing this, Jesus said to him, "Still one thing is lacking to you: sell everything that you have and give to the poor, and you will have treasure in heaven; and come, follow Me."
verses.18:23: When he had heard these things, he was saddened, because he was exceedingly rich.
verses.18:24: Now Jesus, seeing that he had become sad, said, "With what difficulty will those who have wealth enter into the kingdom of God!
verses.18:25: For it is easier for a camel to pass through a needle's eye than for a rich man to enter into the kingdom of God."
verses.18:26: And those who were listening said, "And who can be saved?"
verses.18:27: He said to them, "Things that are impossible with human beings are possible with God."
verses.18:28: Now Peter said, "Look, we have left all things and have followed You."
verses.18:29: And He said to them, "Amen, I tell you, there is no one who has left house, or parents, or brothers, or wife, or children on account of the kingdom of God,
verses.18:30: and will not receive much more in this time, and in the coming age eternal life."
verses.18:31: Now Jesus took the Twelve and said to them, "Look, we are going up to Jerusalem, and all things that have been written through the prophets concerning the Son of Man will be accomplished.
verses.18:32: For He will be handed over to the Gentiles, and mocked, and flogged, and spat upon;
verses.18:33: and after they have flogged Him, they will kill Him, and on the third day He will rise again."
verses.18:34: And they themselves understood none of these things, and this word was hidden from them, and they did not understand what was being said.
verses.18:35: Now it happened, as He was approaching Jericho, that a certain blind man was sitting beside the road, begging.
verses.18:36: And when he heard a crowd passing by, he was asking what this was.
verses.18:37: And they told him that Jesus the Nazarene was passing by.
verses.18:38: And he cried out, saying, "Jesus, Son of David, show mercy to me."
verses.18:39: And those who were going ahead were rebuking him so that he would be silent. Yet he himself kept crying out much more, "Son of David, show mercy to me."
verses.18:40: Now Jesus, standing still, ordered him to be brought to Himself. And when he had approached, He questioned him,
verses.18:41: saying, "What do you want Me to do for you?" And he said, "Lord, that I may see."
verses.18:42: And Jesus said to him, "See again; your faith has saved you."
verses.18:43: And immediately he saw, and he was following Him, magnifying God. And as soon as all the people saw this, they gave praise to God.
verses.19:1: And having entered, He was walking through Jericho.
verses.19:2: And look, there was a man named Zacchaeus; and this man was a chief of the tax collectors, and he himself was rich.
verses.19:3: And he was seeking to see Jesus, who He was, and he could not on account of the crowd, because he was short in stature.
verses.19:4: And running ahead, he climbed into a sycamore tree so that he might see Him, because He was going to pass that way.
verses.19:5: And when He had come to the place, looking up, Jesus saw him and said to him, "Zacchaeus, hurry down, because today I must remain in your house."
verses.19:6: And he hurried down and welcomed Him, rejoicing.
verses.19:7: And when they all saw it, they were grumbling, saying that He had turned aside to lodge with a sinful man.
verses.19:8: Now Zacchaeus, standing, said to the Lord, "Look, half of my goods, Lord, I give to the poor, and if I have cheated anyone of anything, I repay fourfold."
verses.19:9: Jesus said to him, "Today salvation has come about for this house, because he himself is also a son of Abraham.
verses.19:10: For the Son of Man came to seek and to save what had been lost."
verses.19:11: While they were listening to these things, adding further, He spoke a parable, because He was close to Jerusalem and because they supposed that the kingdom of God would immediately be manifested.
verses.19:12: Therefore He said, "A certain man of noble birth went away into a distant region to receive a kingdom for himself and to return.
verses.19:13: And having summoned ten of his servants, he gave them ten minas and said to them, 'Conduct business until I come.'
verses.19:14: Yet his citizens hated him, and they sent an embassy after him, saying, 'We do not wish this man to reign over us.'
verses.19:15: And it happened that he returned, having received the kingdom, and he ordered the servants to whom he had given the money to be summoned, so that he might know how much each one had gained in business.
verses.19:16: Now the first came, saying, 'Master, your mina has acquired ten minas.'
verses.19:17: And he said to him, 'Well done, good servant! Because you were faithful in a small matter, you will have authority over ten cities.'
verses.19:18: And another came, saying, 'Master, your mina has made five minas.'
verses.19:19: And to this one he said, 'You also be over five cities.'
verses.19:20: And another came, saying, 'Master, here is your mina, which I had stored away in a handkerchief;
verses.19:21: for I feared you, because you are a stern man; you take up what you did not set down, and you reap what you did not sow.'
verses.19:22: He says to him, 'From your own mouth I judge you, wicked servant. You knew that I am a stern man, taking up what I did not set down and reaping what I did not sow;
verses.19:23: and why did you not give my money to the bank, so that when I came I would certainly have collected it with interest?'
verses.19:24: And to those standing nearby he said, 'Take the mina away from him, and give it to the one who has ten minas.'
verses.19:25: And they said to him, 'Master, he has ten minas.'
verses.19:26: 'Now I tell you that to everyone who has, it will be given, and he will have an abundance; but from the one who does not have, even what he has will be taken away from him.
verses.19:27: However, those enemies of mine who did not wish me to reign over them, bring them here and put them to death before me.'"
verses.19:28: And when these things had been spoken, He was proceeding ahead, going up to Jerusalem.
verses.19:29: And it happened, when He had drawn near to Bethphage and Bethany, to the mountain called Olivet, He sent two of His disciples,
verses.19:30: saying, "Go into the village that is opposite; upon entering it, you will find a donkey's colt tied, on which no human being has ever sat. Untie it and bring it.
verses.19:31: And if anyone asks you, 'Why are you untying it?' this is what you will say to him: 'Because the Lord desires its service.'"
verses.19:32: Now those who had been sent went away and found the colt standing, just as He told them.
verses.19:33: Now while they were untying the colt, its owners said to them, "Why are you untying the colt?"
verses.19:34: But they said, "Because the Lord needs it."
verses.19:35: And they led it to Jesus. And throwing their garments over the colt, they placed Jesus on it.
verses.19:36: And while He was going along, they were spreading their garments down on the road.
verses.19:37: And when He was already drawing near to the descent of Mount Olivet, all the crowds of disciples, rejoicing, began to praise God with a loud voice for all the deeds of power that they had seen,
verses.19:38: saying, "Blessed is He who comes as King in the name of the Lord! Peace in heaven, and glory in the highest!"
verses.19:39: And some of the Pharisees from the crowds said to Him, "Teacher, rebuke Your disciples."
verses.19:40: To them He Himself said, "I tell you that if these remain silent, the stones will cry out."
verses.19:41: And as soon as He drew near, seeing the city, He wept over it, saying,
verses.19:42: "If you also had known, and indeed on this day of yours, the things that are for your peace! But now they are hidden from your eyes.
verses.19:43: For days will come upon you, and your enemies will surround you with a rampart, and they will surround you and press you in on every side,
verses.19:44: and they will cast you down to the ground, and your children who are in you, and they will not leave in you stone upon stone, because you did not know the time of your visitation."
verses.19:45: And having entered into the temple, He began to drive out those selling in it and those buying,
verses.19:46: saying to them, "It is written, 'My house is a house of prayer,' but you have made it a cave of robbers."
verses.19:47: And He was teaching every day in the temple. Now the chief priests and the scribes and the leader of the people were seeking to destroy Him,
verses.19:48: and they did not find what they might do to Him. For all the people were held in rapt attention, listening to Him.
verses.20:1: And it happened on one of the days, while He was teaching the people in the temple and proclaiming the good news, that the chief priests and the scribes assembled with the elders,
verses.20:2: and they spoke, saying to Him, "Tell us: by what authority do You do these things? Or who is it who gave You this authority?"
verses.20:3: But Jesus, answering, said to them, "I too will ask you one thing. Answer Me:
verses.20:4: Was John's baptism from heaven, or from men?"
verses.20:5: But they were reasoning within themselves, saying, "If we say, 'From heaven,' He will say, 'Why then did you not believe him?'
verses.20:6: But if we say, 'From men,' all the people will stone us; for they are certain that John is a prophet."
verses.20:7: And they answered that they did not know where it was from.
verses.20:8: And Jesus said to them, "Neither do I tell you by what authority I do these things."
verses.20:9: Then He began to tell this parable to the people: "A man planted a vineyard and leased it to tenant farmers, and he himself was abroad for a long time.
verses.20:10: And at the proper time he sent a servant to the growers so that they would give him some of the fruit of the vineyard; yet after beating him, they sent him away empty-handed.
verses.20:11: And he went on to send another servant. Yet beating this one as well and treating him with contempt, they sent him away empty-handed.
verses.20:12: And he went on to send a third; and wounding him also, they threw him out.
verses.20:13: Then the master of the vineyard said, 'What should I do? I will send my beloved son; perhaps, when they see him, they will respect him.'
verses.20:14: When the tenant farmers saw him, they reasoned within themselves, saying, 'This is the heir; let us kill him so that the inheritance may become ours.'
verses.20:15: And after throwing him out of the vineyard, they killed him. What then will the master of the vineyard do to them?
verses.20:16: He will come and destroy those tenant farmers, and give the vineyard to others." Upon hearing this, they said to Him, "Far from it!"
verses.20:17: But He, looking at them, said, "What then is this that is written: 'The stone that the builders rejected, this one has become the head of the corner'?
verses.20:18: Everyone who falls on that stone will be shattered; yet on whomever it falls, it will crush him to pieces."
verses.20:19: And the chief priests and the scribes were seeking to lay hands on Him at that hour, and they feared the people; for they perceived that He had spoken this parable against them.
verses.20:20: And watching closely, they sent spies who pretended to be righteous, so that they might catch Him in His speech in order to hand Him over to the rule and authority of the governor.
verses.20:21: And they questioned Him, saying, "Teacher, we know that You speak and teach rightly, and You do not show partiality, but teach the way of God in truth.
verses.20:22: Is it permitted for us to pay tribute to Caesar, or not?"
verses.20:23: But discerning their deceit, He said to them, "Why do you test Me?
verses.20:24: Show Me a denarius. Whose image and inscription does it have?" Answering, they said to Him, "Caesar's."
verses.20:25: And He said to them, "Therefore give back the things that are Caesar's to Caesar, and the things that are God's to God."
verses.20:26: And they were unable to find fault with His word in the presence of the people; and marveling at His answer, they fell silent.
verses.20:27: Now some of the Sadducees approached, who deny that there is a resurrection, and they questioned Him,
verses.20:28: saying, "Teacher, Moses wrote for us that if anyone's brother dies having a wife, and this man is without children, his brother should take her as his wife and raise up seed for his brother.
verses.20:29: So there were seven brothers; and the first took a wife, and died without children.
verses.20:30: And the next took her, and he also died without a son.
verses.20:31: And the third took her, and likewise all seven as well, and they left no seed and died.
verses.20:32: Last of all, the woman also died.
verses.20:33: In the resurrection, therefore, whose wife among them will she be? For indeed the seven had her as a wife."
verses.20:34: And Jesus said to them, "The sons of this age marry and are given away in marriage;
verses.20:35: yet those who will be considered worthy of that age and of the resurrection from the dead will neither marry nor take wives;
verses.20:36: for neither could they die any longer; for they are equal to the angels, and they are sons of God, since they are sons of the resurrection.
verses.20:37: Now that the dead rise, even Moses showed beside the bush, just as he calls the Lord the God of Abraham, and the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob.
verses.20:38: Yet God is not the God of the dead, but of the living; for all live to Him."
verses.20:39: Then some of the scribes, answering, said to Him, "Teacher, You have spoken well."
verses.20:40: And they no longer dared to question Him about anything.
verses.20:41: Then He said to them, "How do they say that the Christ is the son of David?
verses.20:42: And David himself says in the book of Psalms, 'The Lord said to my Lord: Sit at My right hand,
verses.20:43: until I set Your enemies as a footstool for Your feet.'
verses.20:44: David therefore calls Him Lord; and how is He his son?"
verses.20:45: Now while all the people were listening, He said to His disciples,
verses.20:46: "Watch out for the scribes, who desire to walk in long robes, and love greetings in the marketplace, and the foremost seats in the synagogues, and the foremost places at banquets,
verses.20:47: who devour the houses of widows, making a pretense of a long prayer; these will receive a greater condemnation."
verses.21:1: Now looking up, He saw those who were putting their offerings into the treasury, the rich.
verses.21:2: And He also saw a certain very poor widow putting in two tiny copper coins.
verses.21:3: And He said, "Truly I tell you that this poor widow put in more than everyone.
verses.21:4: For all these put into the offerings of God from what was abundant to them; yet she, from what is lacking to her, put in all of her livelihood that she had."
verses.21:5: And as some were speaking about the temple, that it had been adorned with fine stones and gifts, He said,
verses.21:6: "These things that you see, days will come in which not a stone will be left upon a stone that will not be demolished."
verses.21:7: And they questioned Him, saying, "Master, when will these things be, and what will be the sign when they begin to take place?"
verses.21:8: And He said, "Watch out that you are not led astray; for many will come in My name, saying, 'I am,' and, 'The time has drawn near.' Therefore do not go after them.
verses.21:9: And when you hear of wars and uprisings, do not be terrified; these things must take place first, but the end is not yet immediate."
verses.21:10: Then He was saying to them, "Nation will rise against nation, and kingdom against kingdom.
verses.21:11: And great earthquakes will occur from place to place, and plagues and famines, and there will be terrors from heaven and great signs.
verses.21:12: But before all these things, they will lay their hands upon you and persecute you, handing you over to synagogues and prisons, dragging you to kings and governors on account of My name;
verses.21:13: and it will turn out for you as a testimony.
verses.21:14: Settle it therefore in your hearts not to prepare beforehand how you are to answer;
verses.21:15: for I will give you a mouth and wisdom, which all your adversaries will be unable to resist or contradict.
verses.21:16: And you will be handed over by parents, brothers, relatives, and friends, and they will put some of you to death;
verses.21:17: and you will be hated by everyone on account of My name;
verses.21:18: and not a hair from your head will perish.
verses.21:19: In your endurance you will possess your souls.
verses.21:20: Now when you see Jerusalem surrounded by an army, then know that its desolation has drawn near;
verses.21:21: then let those who are in Judea flee to the mountains, and let those in its midst depart, and let those in the countryside not enter it,
verses.21:22: because these are days of vengeance, so that all things that have been written may be fulfilled.
verses.21:23: But woe to those who are pregnant and those who are nursing in those days! For there will be great distress upon the land, and wrath against this people.
verses.21:24: And they will fall by the edge of the sword, and they will be led as captives into all nations, and Jerusalem will be trampled by the Gentiles until the times of the nations are fulfilled.
verses.21:25: And there will be signs in the sun, moon, and stars, and on the earth distress of the nations because of bewilderment at the roar of the sea and the waves,
verses.21:26: with people withering away from fear and expectation of the things that will come upon the entire world; for the powers of the heavens will be shaken;
verses.21:27: and then they will see the Son of Man coming in a cloud with great power and majesty.
verses.21:28: Now as these things begin to take place, look up and raise your heads, because your redemption is drawing near."
verses.21:29: And He spoke a parable to them: "Look at the fig tree and all the trees:
verses.21:30: when they already produce fruit from themselves, you know that summer is near.
verses.21:31: So you also, when you see these things taking place, know that the kingdom of God is near.
verses.21:32: Amen, I tell you that this generation will not pass away until all things take place.
verses.21:33: Heaven and earth will pass away, yet My words will not pass away.
verses.21:34: Now watch yourselves, so that your hearts may not be weighed down with carousing, drunkenness, and the anxieties of this life, and that day come upon you unexpectedly;
verses.21:35: for like a snare it will come upon all who sit upon the face of the entire earth.
verses.21:36: Stay awake, therefore, praying at all times, so that you may be deemed worthy to escape all these things that are about to happen, and to stand before the Son of Man."
verses.21:37: Now by day He was teaching in the temple, but at night, going out, He would stay on the mountain that is called Olivet.
verses.21:38: And all the people would come to Him early in the morning in the temple to hear Him.
verses.22:1: Now the feast day of Unleavened Bread, which is called Passover, was approaching.
verses.22:2: And the chief priests and the scribes were seeking how they might kill Jesus, yet they feared the people.
verses.22:3: Then Satan entered Judas, who was called by the surname Iscariot, one of the twelve.
verses.22:4: And he went away and spoke with the chief priests and the magistrates about how he might hand Him over to them.
verses.22:5: And they rejoiced and made an agreement to give him money.
verses.22:6: And he gave his promise, and was seeking an opportunity to hand Him over away from the crowds.
verses.22:7: Then the day of Unleavened Bread came, on which it was necessary for the Passover to be killed.
verses.22:8: And He sent Peter and John, saying, "Go, prepare the Passover for us so that we may eat."
verses.22:9: But they said, "Where do You wish us to prepare it?"
verses.22:10: And He said to them, "Look, as you enter the city, a certain man carrying a pitcher of water will meet you; follow him into the house that he enters,
verses.22:11: and you will say to the master of the house, 'The Teacher says to you: Where is the guest room where I may eat the Passover with My disciples?'
verses.22:12: And he himself will show you a large upper room, furnished, and prepare it there."
verses.22:13: So they went and found it as He had said to them, and they prepared the Passover.
verses.22:14: And when the hour had arrived, He reclined at table, and the twelve apostles with Him.
verses.22:15: And He said to them, "With longing I have longed to eat this Passover with you before I suffer.
verses.22:16: For I tell you that from now on I will not eat it until it is fulfilled in the kingdom of God."
verses.22:17: And having taken a cup, He gave thanks and said, "Take it and divide it among yourselves.
verses.22:18: For I tell you that I will not drink from the produce of the vine until the kingdom of God comes."
verses.22:19: And having taken bread, He gave thanks, and broke it, and gave it to them, saying, "This is My body, which is given for you; do this in memory of Me."
verses.22:20: Likewise the cup also, after He had dined, saying, "This is the cup, the new covenant in My blood, which will be poured out for you.
verses.22:21: Yet look, the hand of the one handing Me over is with Me on the table.
verses.22:22: And indeed the Son of Man goes according to what has been determined; yet woe to that man through whom He will be handed over."
verses.22:23: And they began to ask among themselves which of them it was who was about to do this.
verses.22:24: Now a dispute also arose among them about which of them seemed to be the greatest.
verses.22:25: But He said to them, "The kings of the nations exercise dominion over them, and those who hold authority over them are called benefactors.
verses.22:26: With you, however, it is not so; instead, let the one who is greatest among you become like the least, and the one who is leader like the one who serves.
verses.22:27: For who is greater: the one reclining at table, or the one who serves? Is it not the one reclining? Yet I am in your midst like one who serves.
verses.22:28: And you are the ones who have remained with Me in My trials.
verses.22:29: And I bestow on you, just as My Father bestowed on Me, a kingdom,
verses.22:30: so that you may eat and drink at My table in My kingdom, and may sit on thrones, judging the twelve tribes of Israel."
verses.22:31: And the Lord said, "Simon, Simon, look, Satan has demanded you so that he might sift you like wheat;
verses.22:32: yet I Myself have prayed for you so that your faith will not fail; and you, once you have turned back, strengthen your brothers."
verses.22:33: And he said to Him, "Lord, I am prepared to go with You both into prison and to death."
verses.22:34: But He said, "I tell you, Peter, a rooster will not crow today before you three times deny knowing Me." And He said to them,
verses.22:35: "When I sent you without a purse, a satchel, or sandals, did you lack anything?"
verses.22:36: And they said, "Nothing." Therefore He said to them, "But now let the one who has a purse take it, and likewise a satchel; and let the one who has none sell his tunic and buy a sword.
verses.22:37: For I tell you that this which is written must still be fulfilled in Me: 'And He was counted with the wicked.' For indeed those things concerning Me have their end."
verses.22:38: And they said, "Lord, look, there are two swords here." But He said to them, "That is enough."
verses.22:39: And having gone out, He went according to custom to the Mount of Olives, and the disciples also followed Him.
verses.22:40: And when He had arrived at the place, He said to them, "Pray so that you do not enter into temptation."
verses.22:41: And He Himself drew away from them as far as a stone's throw, and kneeling down, He was praying,
verses.22:42: saying, "Father, if You wish, take this cup away from Me; yet let not My will, but Yours, be done."
verses.22:43: Then an angel from heaven appeared to Him, strengthening Him. And being in agony, He was praying at greater length.
verses.22:44: And His sweat became like drops of blood running down onto the ground.
verses.22:45: And when He had risen from prayer and come to His disciples, He found them sleeping from sorrow.
verses.22:46: And He said to them, "Why are you sleeping? Rise, pray, so that you do not enter into temptation."
verses.22:47: While He was still speaking, look, there was a crowd, and the one who was called Judas, one of the twelve, was going ahead of them, and he approached Jesus to kiss Him.
verses.22:48: But Jesus said to him, "Judas, are you handing over the Son of Man with a kiss?"
verses.22:49: Now when those who were around Him saw what was about to happen, they said to Him, "Lord, should we strike with the sword?"
verses.22:50: And one of them struck the servant of the high priest and severed his right ear.
verses.22:51: But Jesus responded and said, "Allow it this far." And when He touched his ear, He healed him.
verses.22:52: Then Jesus said to those who had come to Him, the chief priests and the magistrates of the temple and the elders, "As if against a robber, have you come out with swords and clubs?
verses.22:53: When I was with you daily in the temple, you did not extend your hands against Me; but this is your hour and the authority of darkness."
verses.22:54: Then seizing Him, they led Him to the house of the high priest; Peter, however, was following from a distance.
verses.22:55: Now when a fire had been lit in the middle of the courtyard and they were sitting around it, Peter was in their midst.
verses.22:56: When a certain servant girl saw him sitting by the light and looked intently at him, she said, "This one also was with Him."
verses.22:57: But he denied Him, saying, "Woman, I do not know Him."
verses.22:58: And after a little while, another man, seeing him, said, "You too are one of them." Peter, however, said, "Man, I am not."
verses.22:59: And after an interval of about one hour, a certain other man was insisting, saying, "Truly, this one also was with Him, for he is also a Galilean."
verses.22:60: And Peter said, "Man, I do not know what you are saying." And at once, while he was still speaking, a rooster crowed.
verses.22:61: And turning around, the Lord looked at Peter, and Peter recalled the word of the Lord, as He had said, "Before a rooster crows, you will deny Me three times."
verses.22:62: And going outside, Peter wept bitterly.
verses.22:63: And the men who were holding Him kept mocking Him, beating Him.
verses.22:64: And they blindfolded Him and kept striking His face, and they were questioning Him, saying, "Prophesy! Who is the one who struck You?"
verses.22:65: And blaspheming, they kept speaking many other things against Him.
verses.22:66: And when day arrived, the elders of the people, the chief priests, and the scribes assembled, and they led Him into their council, saying, "If You are the Christ, tell us."
verses.22:67: And He said to them, "If I tell you, you will not believe Me;
verses.22:68: and if I also question you, you will not answer Me, nor will you release Me.
verses.22:69: Yet from now on the Son of Man will be sitting at the right hand of the power of God."
verses.22:70: Then they all said, "Are You then the Son of God?" And He said, "You yourselves say that I am."
verses.22:71: And they said, "Why do we still require testimony? For we ourselves have heard it from His mouth."
verses.23:1: And rising up, the entire multitude of them led Him to Pilate.
verses.23:2: And they began to accuse Him, saying, "We found this man subverting our nation, and forbidding tribute to be given to Caesar, and saying that He is the Christ, a king."
verses.23:3: Now Pilate questioned Him, saying, "Are You the king of the Jews?" But answering, He said, "You say so."
verses.23:4: Then Pilate said to the chief priests and the crowds, "I find no ground for a charge in this man."
verses.23:5: But they grew more insistent, saying, "He stirs up the people, teaching throughout all of Judea, beginning from Galilee all the way to here."
verses.23:6: Now Pilate, hearing of Galilee, asked whether the man was a Galilean.
verses.23:7: And when he learned that He was under Herod's authority, he sent Him over to Herod, who himself also was in Jerusalem in those days.
verses.23:8: Now when Herod saw Jesus, he rejoiced greatly. For he had been desiring for a long time to see Him, because he had heard many things about Him, and he was hoping to see some sign performed by Him.
verses.23:9: And he was questioning Him with many words. But He Himself answered him nothing.
verses.23:10: And the chief priests and the scribes were standing there, persistently accusing Him.
verses.23:11: Then Herod with his troops scorned and mocked Him after clothing Him in a white garment, and sent Him back to Pilate.
verses.23:12: And Herod and Pilate became friends on that very day; for previously they were enemies toward one another.
verses.23:13: Now Pilate, having called together the chief priests, and the magistrates, and the people,
verses.23:14: said to them, "You brought this man to me as one turning the people away, and look, questioning Him before you, I have found no ground for a charge in this man among the things of which you accuse Him.
verses.23:15: But neither has Herod; for I sent you to him, and look, nothing deserving of death has been done by Him.
verses.23:16: Therefore, after punishing Him, I will release Him."
verses.23:18: But the entire crowd cried out all together, saying, "Take this man away, and release to us Barabbas,"
verses.23:19: who had been thrown into prison because of a certain insurrection that had taken place in the city, and for murder.
verses.23:20: Then Pilate spoke to them again, wanting to release Jesus.
verses.23:21: But they kept shouting back, saying, "Crucify, crucify Him!"
verses.23:22: And he said to them a third time, "Why, what evil has this man done? I find no ground for death in Him; therefore I will chastise Him and release Him."
verses.23:23: But they kept pressing on with loud voices, demanding that He be crucified; and their voices were prevailing.
verses.23:24: And Pilate decreed that their petition be carried out.
verses.23:25: And he released to them the one who had been thrown into prison because of murder and insurrection, whom they were asking for; but Jesus he handed over to their will.
verses.23:26: And while they were leading Him, they seized a certain Simon of Cyrene, coming from the countryside, and they placed the cross upon him to carry behind Jesus.
verses.23:27: And a large crowd of the people and of women was following Him, who were wailing and lamenting Him.
verses.23:28: But Jesus, turning to them, said, "Daughters of Jerusalem, do not weep over Me, but weep over yourselves and over your children.
verses.23:29: For look, days will come in which they will say, 'Blessed are the barren, and the wombs that have not given birth, and the breasts that have not nursed.'
verses.23:30: Then they will begin to say to the mountains, 'Fall upon us,' and to the hills, 'Cover us.'
verses.23:31: For if they do these things in the green wood, what will happen in the dry?"
verses.23:32: And two other wicked men were also being led with Him to be put to death.
verses.23:33: And after they came to the place that is called Calvary, there they crucified Him, and the robbers, one on the right and the other on the left.
verses.23:34: Now Jesus was saying, "Father, forgive them, for they do not know what they do." And dividing His garments, they cast lots.
verses.23:35: And the people stood watching, and the rulers along with them were ridiculing Him, saying, "He saved others; let Him save Himself, if this man is the Christ of God, the chosen one."
verses.23:36: And the soldiers also were mocking Him, coming up and offering Him vinegar,
verses.23:37: and saying, "If You are the king of the Jews, save Yourself."
verses.23:38: Now there was also an inscription written above Him in Greek, and Latin, and Hebrew letters: "This is the king of the Jews."
verses.23:39: And one of the robbers who were hanging there was blaspheming Him, saying, "If You are the Christ, save Yourself and us."
verses.23:40: But the other, answering, was rebuking him, saying, "You do not even fear God, since you are under the same condemnation.
verses.23:41: And we indeed justly, for we are receiving what our deeds deserve; but this man has done nothing evil."
verses.23:42: And he was saying to Jesus, "Lord, remember me when You come into Your kingdom."
verses.23:43: And Jesus said to him, "Amen, I tell you, today you will be with Me in paradise."
verses.23:44: Now it was about the sixth hour, and darkness came over the whole earth until the ninth hour.
verses.23:45: And the sun was darkened, and the veil of the temple was torn down the middle.
verses.23:46: And crying out with a loud voice, Jesus said, "Father, into Your hands I entrust My spirit." And saying these things, He breathed His last.
verses.23:47: Now the centurion, seeing what had happened, glorified God, saying, "Truly this man was righteous."
verses.23:48: And the entire crowd of those who were present together at this spectacle and were seeing the things that were happening returned, beating their breasts.
verses.23:49: And all His acquaintances were standing at a distance, and the women who had followed Him from Galilee, seeing these things.
verses.23:50: And look, there was a man named Joseph, who was a council member, a good and righteous man.
verses.23:51: This man had not consented to their counsel and deeds; he was from Arimathea, a city of Judea, and he himself was also waiting for the kingdom of God.
verses.23:52: This man went to Pilate and asked for the body of Jesus,
verses.23:53: and having taken Him down, he wrapped Him in a linen cloth and laid Him in a hewn tomb, in which no one had yet been laid.
verses.23:54: And it was the day of Preparation, and the Sabbath was dawning.
verses.23:55: Now following closely, the women who had come with Him from Galilee saw the tomb and how His body was laid.
verses.23:56: And returning, they prepared spices and ointments; and on the Sabbath they indeed kept still according to the commandment.
verses.24:1: Now on the first day of the week, very early at dawn, they came to the tomb, carrying the spices that they had prepared.
verses.24:2: And they found the stone rolled back from the tomb.
verses.24:3: And having entered, they did not find the body of the Lord Jesus.
verses.24:4: And it happened, while they were dismayed in mind about this, look, two men stood beside them in gleaming clothing.
verses.24:5: Now while they were afraid and lowered their faces to the ground, they said to them, "Why are you seeking the living one among the dead?
verses.24:6: He is not here, but He has risen; remember how He spoke to you when He was still in Galilee,
verses.24:7: saying that the Son of Man must be handed over into the hands of sinful men, and be crucified, and rise again on the third day."
verses.24:9: And having returned from the tomb, they reported all these things to those eleven and to all the rest.
verses.24:10: Now it was Mary Magdalene, and Joanna, and Mary of James, and the other women who were with them, who were saying these things to the apostles.
verses.24:11: And before them those words seemed like nonsense, and they did not believe them.
verses.24:12: But Peter, rising, ran to the tomb; and stooping down, he saw the linen cloths placed by themselves, and he departed, marveling within himself at what had happened.
verses.24:13: And look, two of them were going on that very day to a village that was at a distance of sixty stadia from Jerusalem, named Emmaus.
verses.24:14: And they themselves were speaking with one another about all these things that had occurred.
verses.24:15: And it happened, while they were conversing and inquiring with one another, that Jesus Himself, drawing near, was walking with them.
verses.24:16: Yet their eyes were held so that they would not recognize Him.
verses.24:17: And He said to them, "What are these conversations that you are exchanging with one another while walking, and you are sad?"
verses.24:18: And answering, one of them, whose name was Cleopas, said to Him, "Are You the only stranger in Jerusalem, and have You not known the things that have happened in it during these days?"
verses.24:19: To them He said, "What things?" And they said, "Concerning Jesus the Nazarene, who was a man, a prophet, powerful in deed and word before God and all the people,
verses.24:20: and how our chief priests and rulers handed Him over to a sentence of death, and crucified Him.
verses.24:21: Yet we were hoping that He Himself was about to redeem Israel; and now, in addition to all these things, today is the third day since these things took place.
verses.24:22: Moreover, certain women from among us frightened us, who were at the tomb before daylight,
verses.24:23: and when His body was not found, they came, saying that they had also seen a vision of angels, who say that He lives.
verses.24:24: And some from among us departed to the tomb and found it just as the women said, yet Him they did not find."
verses.24:25: And He said to them, "Oh, foolish ones, and slow in heart to believe in everything that the prophets have spoken!
verses.24:26: Was it not necessary that the Christ suffer these things and thus enter into His glory?"
verses.24:27: And beginning from Moses and all the prophets, He was explaining to them in all the Scriptures the things that were about Himself.
verses.24:28: And they drew near to the village to which they were going, and He made it appear that He was going farther.
verses.24:29: And they pressed Him, saying, "Stay with us, because evening is coming on, and the day has already declined." And He went in with them.
verses.24:30: And it happened, while He was reclining at table with them, that He took the bread, and blessed and broke it, and was handing it to them.
verses.24:31: And their eyes were opened, and they recognized Him; and He Himself vanished from their eyes.
verses.24:32: And they said to one another, "Was not our heart burning inside us while He spoke on the road and opened the Scriptures to us?"
verses.24:33: And rising at that same hour, they returned to Jerusalem, and they found the eleven gathered together and those who were with them,
verses.24:34: saying, "The Lord has truly risen, and has appeared to Simon."
verses.24:35: And they themselves were recounting what had taken place on the road, and how they recognized Him in the breaking of the bread.
verses.24:36: Now while they were speaking these things, Jesus stood in the midst of them and said to them, "Peace to you; it is I, do not be afraid."
verses.24:37: Yet troubled and terrified, they supposed that they were seeing a spirit.
verses.24:38: And He said to them, "Why are you troubled, and why do thoughts rise up in your hearts?
verses.24:39: Look at My hands and feet, that it is I Myself; feel and see, because a spirit does not have flesh and bones, as you see that I have."
verses.24:40: And after He had said this, He showed them His hands and feet.
verses.24:41: Now while they were still not believing and were marveling because of joy, He said, "Do you have anything here to eat?"
verses.24:42: And they offered Him a portion of roasted fish and a honeycomb.
verses.24:43: And when He had eaten in their presence, taking what remained, He gave it to them.
verses.24:44: And He said to them, "These are the words that I spoke to you while I was still with you, that it is necessary for all things written in the Law of Moses, and the Prophets, and the Psalms concerning Me to be fulfilled."
verses.24:45: Then He opened their mind so that they might understand the Scriptures,
verses.24:46: and He said to them, "Thus it is written, and thus it was necessary for the Christ to suffer and to rise again from the dead on the third day,
verses.24:47: and for repentance and forgiveness of sins to be preached in His name among all nations, beginning from Jerusalem.
verses.24:48: Now you are witnesses of these things.
verses.24:49: And I am sending the promise of My Father upon you; as for you, remain in the city until you are clothed with power from on high."
verses.24:50: Then He led them outside to Bethany, and having raised His hands, He blessed them.
verses.24:51: And it happened, while He was blessing them, that He withdrew from them and was being carried into heaven.
verses.24:52: And worshiping, they returned to Jerusalem with great joy,
verses.24:53: and they were continually in the temple, praising and blessing God. Amen.

notes.1:17: The Vulgate renders Greek 'disobedient' as incredulos ('the unbelieving') and 'a prepared people' as plebem perfectam ('a perfected people').
notes.1:28: The Clementine Vulgate translates Greek kecharitomene as gratia plena ('full of grace,' echoing gratiam in 1:30) and includes angelus ('the angel') and benedicta tu in mulieribus ('Blessed are you among women'), phrases omitted in critical Greek editions.
notes.1:35: The Clementine Vulgate includes ex te ('from you'), absent in critical Greek editions, and places the neuter subject quod nascetur ex te sanctum (lit. 'what will be born holy from you') before the predicate 'will be called the Son of God.'
notes.1:37: Literally 'every word will not be impossible with God,' a biblical universal negation meaning 'no word'; Latin verbum ('word,' reflecting Greek rhema) links directly to Mary's 'your word' (verbum tuum) in 1:38.
notes.1:45: Unlike Greek manuscripts that use the third person ('she who believed... spoken to her'), the Clementine Vulgate uses the second person (credidisti... tibi, 'you who have believed... spoken to you').
notes.1:64: The Latin uses a zeugma with a single verb (Apertum est... os ejus, et lingua ejus, lit. 'his mouth was opened, and his tongue'), smoothed here with 'released.'
notes.1:78: Latin viscera misericordiæ literally means 'the inward parts/compassion of the mercy,' and the Clementine Vulgate reads the perfect tense visitavit ('has visited') where critical Greek editions read the future ('will visit'). Latin oriens ('rising,' 'dawn,' 'east') translates Greek anatole.
notes.2:2: The Vulgate reads 'a præside Syriæ Cyrino' ("by Quirinius, governor of Syria"), expressing Quirinius as the agent of the registration rather than the Greek temporal clause ("while Quirinius was governing Syria").
notes.2:14: The Vulgate reads 'hominibus bonæ voluntatis' ("to people of good will"), taking the Greek genitive ('eudokias') as a genitive of quality rather than "those with whom He is pleased."
notes.2:17: The Vulgate reads cognoverunt ("they came to know"), where the Greek reads 'they made known.'
notes.2:22: The Vulgate reads the singular 'purgationis ejus' ("her purification," referring to Mary under Leviticus 12, though Latin 'ejus' is grammatically gender-neutral), whereas critical Greek editions read the plural "their purification."
notes.2:49: Literally "in those [things] that are of My Father" ('in his quæ Patris mei sunt'), a neuter plural expression preserving the Vulgate's openness between "My Father's affairs" and "My Father's house."
notes.3:2: The Vulgate reads plural "principibus sacerdotum" ("high priests") and "verbum Domini" ("the word of the Lord"), whereas many Greek manuscripts read the singular "high priest" and "the word of God."
notes.3:8: The Vulgate reads simply "ne cœperitis dicere" ("do not begin to say"), without the phrase "to yourselves" found in the Greek text.
notes.3:15: The Vulgate uses "existimante" ("thinking" or "supposing") rather than the Greek participle meaning "waiting in expectation."
notes.3:26: The Vulgate preserves the names "Semei," "Joseph," and "Judah" (Juda) here—along with "Joanna" in 3:27 and "Jonah" (Jona) in 3:30—where critical Greek editions read "Semein," "Josech," "Joda," "Joanan," and "Jonam."
notes.3:33: The Vulgate reads "Aram" (Ram) directly between Amminadab and Hezron, matching the Old Testament lineage rather than the two names "Admin" and "Arni" found in critical Greek manuscripts.
notes.4:4: The Vulgate includes the closing clause 'sed in omni verbo Dei' ("but by every word of God"), aligning with the Byzantine Greek tradition and Matthew 4:4, whereas most modern critical Greek editions end the quotation after "bread alone."
notes.4:5: The Vulgate explicitly includes 'diabolus' ("the devil") and 'in montem excelsum' ("onto a high mountain"), matching the Byzantine Greek tradition, whereas many critical Greek manuscripts omit both details in Luke.
notes.4:10: Following the Latin Psalter (Psalm 90:11 [91:11]), the Vulgate uses the perfect tense 'mandavit' ("He has commanded") rather than the future tense found in the Greek text.
notes.4:18: The Vulgate includes 'sanare contritos corde' ("to heal the brokenhearted").
notes.4:19: The Clementine Vulgate adds 'et diem retributionis' ("and the day of retribution") from Isaiah 61:2, which the Greek text of Luke lacks here.
notes.4:44: The Vulgate reads 'Galilææ' ("of Galilee"), matching the Byzantine Greek tradition, whereas many early Greek manuscripts and modern critical editions read "of Judea."
notes.5:5: The Clementine Vulgate reads singular rete ("the net") here and rete eorum ("their net") in 5:6, contrasting with plural retia vestra ("your nets") in 5:4 and differing from the plural Greek text.
notes.5:17: The Clementine Vulgate reads ad sanandum eos ("to heal them"), reflecting the majority Greek tradition rather than critical Greek editions that read "for him to heal."
notes.5:23: Unlike 5:20 (peccata tua, "your sins"), the Clementine Vulgate here omits tua and reads simply Dimittuntur tibi peccata ("Sins are forgiven you").
notes.5:34: Latin filios sponsi ("the sons of the bridegroom") preserves a literal Semitic idiom for wedding attendants and differs slightly from the Greek wording "sons of the bridal chamber."
notes.5:38: The Clementine Vulgate retains et utraque conservantur ("and both are preserved"), which modern critical Greek editions omit here; likewise, 5:39 preserves statim ("immediately") and comparative melius ("better").
notes.6:1: The Clementine Vulgate reads "in sabbato secundo, primo" ("on the second-first Sabbath"), reflecting the rare and debated Greek term deuteroproto omitted by many modern critical Greek editions. It has been variously interpreted as the first Sabbath after the second day of Passover or a Sabbath tied to a festival cycle.
notes.6:28: Vulgate "calumniantibus" specifically means "those who slander" or "falsely accuse," a distinctive Latin rendering where the Greek reads "those who mistreat."
notes.6:35: Vulgate "nihil inde sperantes" ("hoping for nothing from it") unambiguously resolves a debated Greek phrase (meden apelpizontes) that has also been interpreted as "despairing of no one."
notes.6:40: The Vulgate reads "perfectus autem omnis erit, si sit sicut magister ejus" ("everyone will be perfect if he is like his teacher"), making likeness to the teacher the condition for perfection rather than the Greek wording ("everyone, when fully trained, will be like his teacher").
notes.6:48: The Clementine Vulgate reads "fundata enim erat super petram" ("for it had been founded upon the rock"), whereas many modern critical Greek editions read "because it had been well built."
notes.7:9: The Clementine Vulgate includes Amen ("Truly") before "I say to you" (paralleling Matt 8:10), whereas the Greek text of Luke omits it.
notes.7:22: The Vulgate reverses the Greek order ("what you have seen and heard") to "what you have heard and seen" (quae audistis et vidistis), paralleling Matt 11:4.
notes.7:31: The Clementine Vulgate includes the narrative introduction "And the Lord said" (Ait autem Dominus), marking verses 29-30 as Luke's commentary rather than Jesus's speech; many early Greek manuscripts omit this clause.
notes.7:45: The Vulgate reads third-person "from the time she entered" (ex quo intravit), reflecting an ancient textual variant where most Greek manuscripts read first-person ("since I came in").
notes.7:47: Latin quoniam ("for") carries the same debated causal-or-evidential range as the Greek, indicating either the ground or the evidence of her forgiveness; the Vulgate also uses comparative minus ("less") rather than Greek "little."
notes.8:10: The Vulgate reads singular mysterium ("mystery"), whereas the Greek text of Luke has plural "mysteries."
notes.8:25: The Vulgate reads mari ("the sea") rather than Greek "the water," and uses the parenthetical putas ("do you suppose") to render the Greek inferential particle.
notes.8:36: Distinctively, the Vulgate reads a legione ("from the legion"), whereas the Greek text reads "the demon-possessed man."
notes.8:40: The source Latin text prints future erunt, here understood in the past narrative context as the standard Vulgate imperfect erant ("were").
notes.8:49: The Vulgate reads ad principem synagogae ("to the ruler of the synagogue") rather than Greek "from the synagogue ruler's house," and illum ("Him") rather than "the Teacher."
